items.title: Joseph Rene Interview, 1960-04-07
items.q: >> [INTERVIEWER] Charlie Flushes, [INTERVIEWEE] and he began to play, wow, wow, we began to play the blues with that.

ctx.x: of course, they didn't want to give me the credit. I didn't want it, no, huh? Because all I was trying to do, take the ideas, you know, to get ahead of the other fella. I went to the, this must have been back in 1910 or 11, but way back then, got a coconut shell and cut it in half. Because you see, I've seen Buddy Petit, but the first one played, you know, with his derby. He was the first man ever played with a derby, you see, and him and another fella, Frederick Kepage, you all heard talking about Frederick…

and he began to play, wow, wow, we began to play the blues with that. Them fellas used to figure all kinds of items, that's how we used to do, try to out scheme one another, you know. But my brother, he just had a good tone in the horn, and he played clean, and I played nice, straight drums. And that's, in other words, I'd consider my style as a standard style, because the time and the swing, I had the time and I had the swing, you see, and that's good. And that's the thing, I think, you'll always stay in a nice,…
